editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing would mislead a learner. That includes the SabreSwap/NP-hard caveats in [30], the Toffoli "up to six CNOT" claim in [46] and the scheduling caveats in [64]. The one problem is the stage-name headings, which are handled inconsistently. Init, Layout, Translation and Optimization stay in English ("Estágio Init", "Estágio Translation"), but the routing heading is translated as "Estágio de roteamento" [28], while the body of [29] keeps "*Routing*" in English and [63] keeps "Scheduling". A small calque in [40] ("especialmente importantes para destacar") also reads stiffly.

examples.suggested: Estágio Routing (to match Estágio Init/Layout/Translation/Optimization and *Routing* in [29]), or translate every stage name the same way
examples.why: Only the routing heading is translated. The other stage headings stay in English, and [29] calls the same stage *Routing*, so the reader sees two names for one stage.

examples.source: Two special cases are especially important to highlight, and help illustrate what this stage does.
examples.translation: Dois casos especiais são especialmente importantes para destacar e ajudam a ilustrar o que este estágio faz.
examples.suggested: Vale destacar dois casos especiais, que ajudam a ilustrar o que este estágio faz.
examples.why: This copies the English sentence structure word for word and doubles 'especiais/especialmente'. A native technical writer would rephrase it.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing would mislead a learner. "matrizes de densidade", "canais" and "medições gerais" are correct, and the description of the course scope in [9] keeps the comparison "mais ampla do que aquelas discutidas em Fundamentos". The only problem is that two headings copy English title case: "Visão Geral" in [2] and "Badge Conquistado" in [14]. Portuguese sentence-case headings would be "Visão geral" and "Badge conquistado".

examples.why: This copies English title case. Portuguese headings capitalize only the first word.
This copies English title case. Portuguese headings use sentence case.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Nothing would mislead a learner: the variational bound, the caveat in [178] that a measured energy can come out below the exact value, and the negative reaction energy all survive intact. There are three smaller problems. First, in the fill-in-the-blank exercise ([99]–[113]) the sentence is in Portuguese, but the word bank and answer key stay in English ("classical optimizer", "molecular Hamiltonian", "quantum computing"), except [102], which is translated as "energia do estado fundamental"; the learner is left mixing languages and the key no longer matches the bank. Second, a few sentences are stiff or ungrammatical: [134] drops the "em" in "que um único qubit pode estar", [241] reads "Para emaranhamento de qubits" where "Para emaranhar qubits" is needed, and [142] has no subject in "Começando do ponto... sempre produzirá um anel". Third, there are small inconsistencies: "primitivas do IBM Quantum" ([120]) vs "da IBM Quantum" ([124]), and "estado tentativo" / "estados quânticos de tentativa" vs the "função tentativa" used everywhere else.

examples.why: The word bank for a Portuguese fill-in-the-blank stays in English, yet the sibling entry [102] is translated. The answer key [109]-[113] also stays English, so the exercise mixes languages inconsistently.

examples.source: the possible quantum states a single qubit can be in
examples.translation: dos possíveis estados quânticos que um único qubit pode estar
examples.suggested: dos possíveis estados quânticos em que um único qubit pode estar
examples.why: The required preposition "em" is missing, which makes the sentence ungrammatical.
"Para" followed by a noun breaks the parallel infinitive structure of the other answer options.

examples.source: Starting from the point $(0,0,1)$ and rotating around one axis will always yield a ring.
examples.translation: Começando do ponto $(0,0,1)$ e girando em torno de um eixo, sempre produzirá um anel.
examples.suggested: Partir do ponto $(0,0,1)$ e girar em torno de um eixo sempre produzirá um anel.
examples.why: This calques the English gerund subject, so the Portuguese verb ends up with no subject.

examples.translation: incluindo as primitivas da IBM Quantum

examples.why: Inconsistent with [120] "primitivas do IBM Quantum"; use one gender for the product name throughout.
